questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of cloud computing compared with on-premises infrastructure?
options: Increased time required to provision new resources
A requirement to maintain long-term contracts with hardware vendors
Replacing capital expenditures (CapEx) with variable operating expenses (OpEx)
A need to purchase servers years in advance
questions.explanation: One of the main benefits of the cloud is replacing large upfront hardware investments (CapEx) with pay-as-you-go operating expenses (OpEx), so you pay only for the resources you consume.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the concept of elasticity in AWS?
options: The ability to encrypt data automatically
The ability to automatically increase or decrease resources based on demand
The ability to generate financial reports automatically
The ability to migrate data between Regions at no cost
questions.explanation: Elasticity is the ability of a system to automatically scale resources up or down according to demand, helping avoid both wasted capacity and insufficient capacity.

questions.text: What is an AWS Region in the AWS global infrastructure?
options: A geographic area that contains multiple isolated Availability Zones
questions.explanation: An AWS Region is a geographic location made up of multiple Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone contains one or more independent data centers.

questions.text: According to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for security OF the cloud?
options: Neither party; it is the end user's responsibility
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud, including the physical infrastructure, hardware, and virtualization layer. Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud, including their data, configurations, and access management.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used to manage users, groups, and access permissions for resources in an AWS account?
questions.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is used to create and manage users, groups, roles, and policies that control access to AWS resources.

questions.text: What does AWS recommend for securing the root user of an AWS account?
options: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) and avoid using the root user for routine tasks
Delete the root user as soon as the account is created
Share the root credentials with the entire IT team
Use the root user for all day-to-day administrative tasks
questions.explanation: AWS recommends protecting the root user with MFA, using it only for tasks that absolutely require root-level access, and using IAM identities with appropriately limited permissions for everyday work.

questions.text: Which feature adds an extra layer of security to an IAM user's sign-in beyond a password?
questions.explanation: MFA requires an additional authentication factor, such as a code generated by an authenticator application, in addition to the password, which improves account security.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used for object storage, such as storing images and backup files?
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) is AWS object storage. It is commonly used to store files such as images, videos, and backups.

questions.text: What is Amazon EC2?
options: A service that provides on-demand compute capacity through virtual servers
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) provides virtual servers called instances that can be launched, resized, and terminated on demand.

questions.text: Which AWS service lets you create a logically isolated virtual network for resources such as EC2 instances?
questions.explanation: Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch resources in a virtual network that you define.

questions.text: Which AWS service is a fully managed NoSQL database?
questions.explanation: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed key-value NoSQL database that provides fast and predictable performance at any scale.

questions.text: Which AWS tool helps estimate the monthly cost of an architecture before it is implemented?
questions.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator lets you estimate the cost of AWS services before building an architecture, helping with financial planning.

questions.text: A startup is planning to launch a new application on AWS and needs a tool that can estimate costs in detail while considering different service configurations, Regions, and pricing models. Which AWS tool is best suited for this purpose and provides the flexibility to model different scenarios before deployment?
questions.explanation: AWS Pricing Calculator lets users create detailed cost estimates for AWS architectures. It provides the flexibility to add and configure multiple services, select different Regions, instance types, storage options, and pricing models, making it easier to compare scenarios and plan costs before deployment.
questions.hint: Think of the tool that lets you simulate and plan the cost of new AWS infrastructure or services before you start using them.
optionRationales: AWS Pricing Calculator lets users create detailed cost estimates for AWS architectures. It provides the flexibility to add and configure multiple services, select different Regions, instance types, storage options, and pricing models, making it easier to compare scenarios and plan costs before deployment.

AWS Cost Explorer is a tool for visualizing and analyzing AWS costs and usage after deployment. It helps you understand past spending and identify trends, but it is not designed to estimate the cost of a new architecture before implementation.

AWS Budgets lets you define custom budgets for AWS costs and usage and receive alerts when your cost or usage exceeds, or is forecast to exceed, the limits you set. Although it is a cost-management tool, its focus is controlling and monitoring spending after deployment rather than estimating a new architecture up front.

AWS Trusted Advisor provides real-time recommendations to optimize cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, and operational excellence for existing AWS resources. It is not a tool for estimating the cost of a new architecture or comparing pricing scenarios before deployment.

questions.text: A media company wants to design its systems on AWS so the architecture can automatically recover from hardware failures or network disruptions with as little impact as possible. According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar specifically focuses on a system's ability to mitigate and recover from disruptions?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar focuses on a workload's ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently and to recover from failures automatically.
questions.hint: Think of the technical term associated with system stability, high availability, and disaster recovery planning.
optionRationales: The Reliability pillar focuses on a workload's ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently and to recover from failures automatically.
The Security pillar focuses on protecting data, systems, and sensitive assets and on controlling identities and access privileges, rather than primarily addressing structural hardware resilience.
The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on the efficient and structured use of computing resources to meet changing technical demand requirements.
The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on avoiding unnecessary spending and managing cloud financial resources economically.

questions.text: A traditional hospital keeps confidential patient records on local servers. To expand capacity, the organization decides to use AWS for public appointment-scheduling applications while keeping confidential data isolated in its private on-premises data center. Which cloud deployment model describes this mixed architecture?
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure or private clouds with public cloud services and resources, allowing data and applications to interact across both environments.
questions.hint: Consider the model that acts as a bridge between an organization's local physical infrastructure and the global AWS ecosystem.
optionRationales: A private cloud model operates exclusively inside dedicated infrastructure for a single organization and does not use shared public-cloud services from AWS.
A hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure or private clouds with public cloud services and resources, allowing data and applications to interact across both environments.
A public cloud provides compute, networking, and storage resources to customers over the internet and is fully managed by a cloud provider such as AWS.
A community cloud is infrastructure shared by specific organizations that have common interests and compliance requirements, which differs from integrating on-premises infrastructure with AWS.

questions.text: Before migrating to AWS, a retail chain had to make large upfront investments in physical servers, routers, and cooling systems that took months to deliver and install. In the AWS Cloud, those heavy upfront capital costs were replaced with variable monthly payments based only on actual usage. How is this financial transition classified in accounting terms?
options: A shift from capital expenditures (CapEx) to operating expenses (OpEx).
A complete replacement of fixed costs with long-term amortized investment expenses.
The complete elimination of operating expenses (OpEx) and corporate service fees.
A shift from operating expenses (OpEx) to capital expenditures (CapEx).
questions.explanation: Cloud computing allows organizations to replace capital expenditures, such as large investments in physical hardware, with operating expenses based on the ongoing consumption of services, reducing upfront financial risk.
questions.hint: Focus on the accounting term for money spent on ongoing operations and utility-like consumption, as opposed to purchasing fixed assets and property.
optionRationales: This statement reverses the concept because it suggests that the organization increased its purchases of fixed assets while reducing flexible service-based costs.

Cloud computing allows organizations to replace capital expenditures, such as large investments in physical hardware, with operating expenses based on the ongoing consumption of services, reducing upfront financial risk.
The cloud pay-as-you-go model focuses on current, flexible consumption expenses rather than static accounting lines for long-term asset amortization.
Operating expenses are not eliminated. They become the primary billing model in the cloud as organizations pay for utilities and services consumed each month.

questions.text: A startup wants to launch a global application and ensure that users in Tokyo, London, and São Paulo can access static media files with the lowest possible network latency. Which component of the AWS global infrastructure caches copies of these files at edge points of presence distributed around the world?
questions.explanation: Edge Locations are edge points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache static content close to end users around the world, significantly reducing latency.
questions.hint: Look for the edge-network component designed specifically for fast content delivery at the boundary of the global infrastructure.
optionRationales: Availability Zones are isolated data-center groupings within a Region that provide local high availability; they are not primarily global edge caching points.
Edge Locations are edge points of presence used by services such as Amazon CloudFront to cache static content close to end users around the world, significantly reducing latency.
A Region is a physical geographic area made up of multiple isolated Availability Zones and serves as a primary location for provisioning large-scale AWS resources.
Local Zones extend selected AWS services such as compute and storage into specific metropolitan areas for very low local latency. They are not global CDN caching locations.

questions.text: While planning the migration of a legacy ERP system to the cloud, an engineering team determines that the current software already meets business requirements and does not need code changes. The team chooses to move the application from on-premises servers to Amazon EC2 instances on AWS without making structural modifications. Which of the 6 Rs migration strategies describes this approach?
questions.explanation: Rehosting, commonly called Lift-and-Shift, moves applications and servers from an on-premises environment directly to the cloud without changing the application code or architecture.
questions.hint: Think of the term that literally means moving an application to a new host, commonly known in IT as Lift-and-Shift.
optionRationales: Replatforming involves small optimizations or component changes, such as moving from an on-premises database to Amazon RDS, without changing the core application. That differs from a direct move with no changes.
Rehosting, commonly called Lift-and-Shift, moves applications and servers from an on-premises environment directly to the cloud without changing the application code or architecture.

Refactoring involves rewriting significant portions of the application code or architecture to take fuller advantage of cloud-native and serverless capabilities, which requires substantially more effort.
Repurchasing means replacing the current application with a different commercial software product, commonly by adopting a Software as a Service (SaaS) platform.

questions.text: A solutions architect is reviewing the operational workflows of an airline in the cloud. The architect wants to automate daily tasks such as creating backups and security alerts and ensure that the team can evolve infrastructure through repeatable infrastructure-as-code (IaC). According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar directly addresses these operational best practices?
questions.explanation: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and on continually improving supporting processes and procedures.
questions.hint: This pillar focuses on day-to-day change management, routine automation, and continuous learning from operational failures.
optionRationales: The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and on continually improving supporting processes and procedures.
The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing the environmental impacts of running cloud workloads, including reducing physical energy consumption in data centers.
The Reliability pillar addresses resilience and the ability to mitigate failures in active systems so infrastructure continues to operate correctly.
The Cost Optimization pillar helps organizations understand where financial resources are being spent and how to remove unnecessary costs from the monthly bill.

questions.text: An e-commerce retailer wants to expand its technology infrastructure by using a cloud-computing benefit that reduces the time needed to provision new servers, databases, and analytics tools from weeks to just minutes. This ability to innovate quickly and reduce time to market for new products represents which core cloud benefit?
questions.explanation: Agility in cloud computing refers to how quickly new technology resources can be made available to developers, greatly reducing the time and cost of experimentation and innovation.
questions.hint: Think of the word associated with speed, the ability to change direction quickly, and the ease of testing new software ideas without the bureaucracy of purchasing physical hardware.
optionRationales: Elasticity is the ability to expand or contract computing resources automatically as immediate traffic demand changes; it is not primarily about the speed of experimenting with new types of services.
Agility in cloud computing refers to how quickly new technology resources can be made available to developers, greatly reducing the time and cost of experimentation and innovation.
Economies of scale are the financial benefit that allows AWS to offer lower prices because it purchases and operates hardware at massive global scale.
High availability means designing a system to remain online and accessible even when isolated physical infrastructure components fail.

questions.text: A junior network engineer is studying the AWS global infrastructure while designing a highly available application. The engineer learns that, to protect servers from local environmental disasters such as floods or fires, data centers are grouped into physically isolated facilities with independent power, cooling, and networking within the same Region. What does AWS call each of these isolated physical groupings?
questions.explanation: An Availability Zone (AZ) consists of one or more discrete, isolated data centers within a geographic Region that are connected through ultra-low-latency fiber networks to provide local fault tolerance.
questions.hint: Look for the term whose common acronym, AZ, represents a physical and electrical boundary designed for resilience and local high availability.
optionRationales: Edge Locations are edge facilities primarily used by CDN services such as CloudFront to cache content; they are not data-center complexes used to host core resources for high availability.

An Availability Zone (AZ) consists of one or more discrete, isolated data centers within a geographic Region that are connected through ultra-low-latency fiber networks to provide local fault tolerance.
Local Zones place selected compute and storage services close to specific metropolitan areas for very low local latency and operate as extensions of a parent Region.
Regions are large independent geographic areas that contain multiple Availability Zones and represent a higher-level boundary for geopolitical and climate isolation.

questions.text: A large technology company serves thousands of enterprise customers around the world. Because AWS purchases enormous volumes of hardware components, servers, and energy globally, its unit operating costs fall substantially, allowing cloud-service prices to be reduced for customers over time. Which cloud advantage describes this financial effect?
options: Stopping spending caused by guessing compute capacity.
Benefiting from massive economies of scale.
Completely replacing operating expenses with capital expenditures.
questions.explanation: Economies of scale allow AWS to achieve lower ownership and operating costs because it manages resources at enormous scale and can pass part of that efficiency on to customers through lower prices.
questions.hint: Think of the economic concept in which producing, buying, or operating at massive scale lowers the per-unit cost.
optionRationales: Cloud computing does the opposite, converting rigid capital investments (CapEx) into flexible, variable consumption expenses (OpEx).
Economies of scale allow AWS to achieve lower ownership and operating costs because it manages resources at enormous scale and can pass part of that efficiency on to customers through lower prices.

Avoiding capacity guessing is a real cloud benefit related to elasticity and preventing underutilization or insufficient capacity, but it does not describe lower unit prices produced by massive purchasing power.
Speed and agility describe how quickly teams can provision technology resources and release software, not the macroeconomic billing effect of large-scale purchasing.

questions.text: The compliance team at a digital bank determines that certain legacy billing and internal-processing applications must not be moved to the public cloud because of strict data-sovereignty and physical-custody regulations. The bank keeps these workloads on its own local servers and private data centers under full corporate control. Which cloud deployment model describes this local configuration?
questions.explanation: A private-cloud or on-premises model refers to an organization managing and running proprietary IT resources in physical facilities dedicated exclusively to that organization.
questions.hint: Think of the traditional IT term for servers and infrastructure installed and managed inside the organization's own facilities.
optionRationales: A public cloud delivers on-demand services over the internet, with the underlying physical infrastructure owned and operated by a third-party provider such as AWS.
A private-cloud or on-premises model refers to an organization managing and running proprietary IT resources in physical facilities dedicated exclusively to that organization.
A hybrid cloud requires active integration and connectivity between private on-premises environments and public-cloud resources, which is not described by the strictly isolated local scenario.
Multi-tenancy is a technical property of sharing underlying physical infrastructure among multiple public-cloud customers, which is the opposite of a dedicated local private environment.

questions.text: A solutions architect is reviewing the design of a high-performance financial application. The team wants compute costs to decrease automatically overnight when user traffic falls close to zero and scale back up smoothly in the morning to support transaction peaks. Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on matching resource supply to real demand at the lowest possible cost?
questions.explanation: The Cost Optimization pillar includes practices for understanding cloud spending, eliminating financial waste through right-sizing, and matching resources to actual elastic demand.
questions.hint: Focus on the pillar whose name directly describes the financial-engineering effort to avoid unnecessary cloud spending.
optionRationales: The Cost Optimization pillar includes practices for understanding cloud spending, eliminating financial waste through right-sizing, and matching resources to actual elastic demand.
The Reliability pillar focuses on technical stability, hardware resilience, and failure recovery so a system remains available; it does not directly govern commercial billing.
The Operational Excellence pillar addresses continuous improvement of processes and automation of routine support and engineering tasks.
The Performance Efficiency pillar focuses on selecting and using computing resources efficiently to maintain the required performance as workloads change.

questions.text: While modernizing a government certificate portal, leadership decides to discontinue an old locally hosted corporate email application. Instead of migrating the physical servers, the organization subscribes to a fully managed third-party cloud service delivered as SaaS, where employees use the ready-made solution through a browser. Which migration strategy describes this replacement?
questions.explanation: Repurchasing means moving to a different product or commercial model, commonly replacing a legacy licensed application with a third-party managed Software as a Service (SaaS) solution.
questions.hint: Think of the strategy associated with buying or subscribing to a replacement product, such as exchanging traditional software licensing for a ready-to-use SaaS service.
optionRationales: Rehosting simply moves existing local applications and virtual servers to cloud infrastructure such as Amazon EC2 without changing their core software or commercial model.
Repurchasing means moving to a different product or commercial model, commonly replacing a legacy licensed application with a third-party managed Software as a Service (SaaS) solution.
Retiring means identifying obsolete systems that no longer provide business value and shutting them down permanently.
Replatforming introduces limited infrastructure optimizations, such as changing a database engine or managed component, without replacing the application with a SaaS product.

questions.text: A German automotive company wants to expand its operations by creating workloads in the AWS Cloud. Its governance committee requires compute instances and transactional databases to remain strictly within European geographic boundaries to meet GDPR data-protection requirements. Which component of the AWS global infrastructure defines this political and geographic boundary?
questions.explanation: An AWS Region is an isolated physical geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones. Choosing a specific Region, such as Frankfurt, determines the primary geographic location in which regional resources are created and supports data-residency requirements.
questions.hint: Think of the highest-level geographic component selected in the AWS console to determine where regional resources are created.
optionRationales: Edge Locations cache and deliver content near internet users and do not serve as the primary legal boundary for residency of application servers and databases.

An AWS Region is an isolated physical geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones. Choosing a specific Region, such as Frankfurt, determines the primary geographic location in which regional resources are created and supports data-residency requirements.
Local Zones extend selected compute and storage capabilities close to specific metropolitan areas for very low latency, while the broader geographic and data-residency boundary is the parent Region.
Availability Zones divide a Region internally into isolated groups of data centers for high availability and remain inside the Region's geographic boundary.

questions.text: A solutions architect is designing an e-commerce web application on AWS according to the AWS Well-Architected Framework. The architect wants continuous log auditing, encryption of data at rest and in transit, strict employee-access privileges, and automated protection of the network perimeter against attacks. Which Well-Architected pillar covers these technical controls?
questions.explanation: The Security pillar focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets through controls such as encryption, least-privilege identity management, logging, detection, and network protection.
questions.hint: Think of the pillar whose core purpose is reducing cyber risk, protecting corporate data from exposure, and controlling legitimate identities and access.
optionRationales: The Reliability pillar focuses on high availability, resilience, and recovery from failures in active systems rather than encryption and identity controls.
The Security pillar focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets through controls such as encryption, least-privilege identity management, logging, detection, and network protection.
The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on operating workloads effectively, automating routine processes, and continually improving operational procedures.
The Cost Optimization pillar focuses on eliminating unnecessary cloud spending and improving financial efficiency.

questions.text: A large insurance company operates hundreds of complex virtual servers on premises. During a financial feasibility study for migration to AWS, the CFO learns that cloud adoption will replace millions of dollars in upfront spending based on static capacity forecasts with small, granular variable charges based on actual on-demand consumption. Which traditional business problem does this cloud characteristic help reduce?
options: Slow global media-delivery networks through Edge Locations.
The need to manually patch AWS KMS encryption keys in relational databases.
Mandatory sharing of physical storage media among competing companies in a private cloud.
Waste from overprovisioning or insufficient capacity caused by guessing infrastructure demand.
questions.explanation: In traditional on-premises environments, organizations often buy excess hardware to prepare for future peaks, leaving servers idle and wasting capital. Cloud elasticity and on-demand consumption reduce the need to guess capacity in advance.
questions.hint: Think of the cloud benefit that lets infrastructure supply track actual demand more closely instead of purchasing hardware based on uncertain forecasts.
optionRationales: Internet edge latency is addressed by CDN services such as CloudFront and is not the accounting problem described by the scenario.

In traditional on-premises environments, organizations often buy excess hardware to prepare for future peaks, leaving servers idle and wasting capital. Cloud elasticity and on-demand consumption reduce the need to guess capacity in advance.
KMS key management and other logical security controls belong to security operations, not to the financial problem of static capacity planning.
Private clouds run dedicated infrastructure for a single organization and the scenario is not describing forced multi-tenant storage sharing.

questions.text: A multinational company plans to migrate its entire IT environment to AWS. To guide this digital transformation and organize strategic planning, leadership adopts the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF). The executive committee wants to focus specifically on modernizing organizational structures, developing new skills for technology teams, and managing cultural change. Which AWS CAF perspective addresses these areas?
questions.explanation: The People perspective of the AWS CAF helps bridge technology and business by focusing on culture, organizational change management, organizational structure, and development of the skills and competencies required for cloud adoption.
questions.hint: Focus on the AWS CAF perspective dedicated to the human side of transformation, including team development, leadership, and cultural change.
optionRationales: The People perspective of the AWS CAF helps bridge technology and business by focusing on culture, organizational change management, organizational structure, and development of the skills and competencies required for cloud adoption.
The Governance perspective focuses on IT portfolio management, program and project management, and control of corporate costs and benefits rather than directly on workforce cultural development.
The Platform perspective focuses on architecture design, cloud-environment provisioning, and optimization of technical compute and networking solutions.
The Business perspective aligns cloud investments with strategic business goals, monetization, financial targets, and market outcomes.

questions.text: A backend developer wants to provision a cloud environment for a REST API and needs the highest possible level of administrative flexibility, including full control over the operating system choice, such as Ubuntu Linux or Windows Server, command-line access through SSH or RDP, and manual management of virtual disks. Which cloud service model provides this level of control?
questions.explanation: IaaS models such as Amazon EC2 provide fundamental virtual compute, networking, and block-storage resources and give customers the greatest level of control over operating systems and installed software.
questions.hint: Think of the service model in which the provider supplies the fundamental infrastructure building blocks while you remain responsible for administering the operating system and installed software.
optionRationales: PaaS models such as AWS Elastic Beanstalk abstract much of the operating system and infrastructure management so developers can focus primarily on deploying application code.
SaaS delivers complete ready-to-use business applications through interfaces such as web browsers and provides no direct control over the underlying network or servers.

IaaS models such as Amazon EC2 provide fundamental virtual compute, networking, and block-storage resources and give customers the greatest level of control over operating systems and installed software.
FaaS, such as event-driven serverless compute with AWS Lambda, abstracts server management and runs functions without giving customers administrative control over the underlying operating system.

questions.text: A food-delivery startup uses Amazon EC2 instances to host its main application. During lunch and dinner hours, the system experiences a massive increase in simultaneous customer requests. The infrastructure team wants to ensure the application can perfectly match this variable demand. What technical term specifically describes a system's ability to automatically expand and reduce computing resources in real time to closely match workload fluctuations?
questions.explanation: Cloud elasticity is the ability to dynamically and automatically increase or decrease computing resources in direct response to fluctuating traffic demand, helping avoid waste from idle resources.
questions.hint: The word refers to a physical property of a material that stretches and contracts immediately according to the force applied to it.
optionRationales: High availability ensures that a system remains online and accessible even if specific hardware components fail, but it does not describe elastic adjustment of compute capacity.
Static scalability refers to expanding resources through fixed, manual, long-term planning, which does not respond well to workload changes that occur over only a few hours.
Cloud elasticity is the ability to dynamically and automatically increase or decrease computing resources in direct response to fluctuating traffic demand, helping avoid waste from idle resources.
Fault tolerance is the property that lets an application continue operating without performance degradation even when partial mechanical failures or data-center power failures occur.

questions.text: A junior IT analyst wants to perform a preventive review of the company's AWS account to identify possible optimizations. The analyst is looking for a tool that acts as an automated online consultant, continuously evaluating active resources against AWS best practices and issuing recommendations across categories such as Cost Optimization, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, and Fault Tolerance. Which tool best fits this advisory scope?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor acts as a real-time cloud consultant that inspects the account environment and provides dashboard recommendations to help optimize cost, close security gaps, improve performance, and increase resilience.
questions.hint: Focus on the AWS console tool whose name can be understood as a 'trusted advisor.'
optionRationales: AWS Trusted Advisor acts as a real-time cloud consultant that inspects the account environment and provides dashboard recommendations to help optimize cost, close security gaps, improve performance, and increase resilience.

OpsCenter centralizes operational work items (OpsItems) so engineers can investigate software failures and infrastructure incidents, but it is not a broad best-practices auditing service for the AWS environment.

AWS Compute Optimizer uses machine learning with a narrower focus on rightsizing resources such as EC2 instance families, EBS volumes, and Lambda functions rather than broad categories such as edge security or network firewall rules.
AWS Pricing Calculator is a web-based tool used to model architectures and estimate theoretical costs before resources are provisioned; it does not scan active infrastructure in an account.

questions.text: The Chief Sustainability Officer (CSO) of an e-commerce organization has been tasked with reducing the carbon footprint generated by the company's technology operations. Under the Sustainability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework and the Shared Responsibility Model as applied to sustainability, which of the following tasks is an exclusive and direct responsibility of AWS?
options: Configure application code to optimize vCPU and RAM consumption during background processing.
Select Amazon EC2 instances based on highly energy-efficient chips such as AWS Graviton to run microservices.
Manage the efficiency of the physical data-center lifecycle, supply renewable energy to facilities, and environmentally dispose of obsolete hardware.
Implement Amazon S3 data lifecycle policies to archive obsolete files in cold tiers such as Glacier Deep Archive.
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for sustainability OF the cloud. This includes maximizing the energy efficiency of the shared global infrastructure, investing in renewable energy for data centers, and managing physical cooling and component recycling.
questions.hint: Remember that AWS focuses on ecological efficiency and sustainable operation of the physical structures and global data-center hardware.
optionRationales: Optimizing application code and the execution efficiency of software built and hosted in the cloud is a customer responsibility for sustainability IN the cloud.
Selecting instance families, appropriate sizing, and logical hardware architecture choices is the responsibility of the cloud customer when designing applications.

AWS is responsible for sustainability OF the cloud. This includes maximizing the energy efficiency of the shared global infrastructure, investing in renewable energy for data centers, and managing physical cooling and component recycling.
Managing logical data lifecycle to reduce unnecessary storage of cold data is under the customer's governance in the cloud.

questions.text: A department-store chain plans to migrate its mobile application to AWS. In an executive meeting, the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) emphasizes that the biggest advantage will not only be financial, but also the company's ability to deploy servers, microservices, and new global features in minutes through clicks or infrastructure as code, allowing the business to respond quickly to market changes and test new ideas with low risk. Which core cloud benefit is the CTO describing?
questions.explanation: Cloud agility gives teams nearly immediate access to IT resources, dramatically reducing the time required to launch innovations and shortening time to market while encouraging rapid product experimentation.
questions.hint: Look for the concept associated with innovation speed, strategic flexibility, and a major reduction in the time required to launch new products.
optionRationales: Economies of scale are primarily a cost benefit created by AWS's massive global purchasing power, which can reduce unit costs and service prices over time.
Technical reliability helps infrastructure remain operational and mitigate failures through resilience and geographic high availability.

Cloud agility gives teams nearly immediate access to IT resources, dramatically reducing the time required to launch innovations and shortening time to market while encouraging rapid product experimentation.
High availability focuses on keeping systems accessible even when specific physical server components fail.

questions.text: A startup has just created its first AWS account and the responsible engineer wants to ensure that the identity with full administrative privileges is not used for everyday work. According to AWS best practices, what should be done with the root user immediately after the account is initially configured?
options: Share the root user's password with the entire development team to speed up deployments.
Create a public root access key and embed it in the application's source code.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA), secure the credentials, and create IAM identities for daily tasks.
Permanently delete the root user from the AWS console to reduce compromise risk.
questions.explanation: This approach protects the root user from unauthorized access and ensures operational activities follow the principle of least privilege through IAM.
questions.hint: Best practices recommend isolating the identity with absolute privileges and using restricted identities for normal routines.
optionRationales: This approach protects the root user from unauthorized access and ensures operational activities follow the principle of least privilege through IAM.
Sharing root credentials severely violates auditing and security principles and greatly increases the risk of total environment compromise.
The root user is the fundamental owner of the account and cannot be deleted; it is still required for a small number of specific billing and account-management tasks.
Exposing root access keys is a dangerous practice that can give external attackers complete control of AWS resources.

questions.text: A financial institution hosts virtual servers on Amazon EC2 and wants to understand the AWS Shared Responsibility Model. Under this model, which of the following activities is the customer's direct responsibility for security IN the cloud?
options: Perform physical maintenance on rack servers located in AWS data centers.
Install operating-system patches and security updates on the guest operating system of the EC2 instance.
Ensure the environmentally safe disposal of damaged physical storage media.
Update the hypervisor software that manages virtualization of the physical resources.
questions.explanation: Because the customer has administrative control over an EC2 instance, the customer is responsible for managing the guest operating system, installed software, and the associated patches and updates.
questions.hint: The customer manages what they configure or install logically inside their account and virtual servers.
optionRationales: Because the customer has administrative control over an EC2 instance, the customer is responsible for managing the guest operating system, installed software, and the associated patches and updates.
Physical security, including underlying hardware and facility perimeter controls, is an AWS responsibility.
The hypervisor belongs to the underlying infrastructure layer managed by AWS as part of security OF the cloud.
Destroying and recycling failed or obsolete physical hardware in AWS data centers is an AWS responsibility.

questions.text: An AWS IAM administrator needs to grant read access to an Amazon S3 bucket for a partner application running in an external AWS account. To allow the third-party application to assume a secure temporary identity without long-term credentials, which IAM component should be configured?
questions.explanation: IAM roles provide temporary, dynamically issued permissions that expire automatically, making them ideal for securely delegating access to services or external accounts.
questions.hint: Consider the resource that issues temporary tokens and does not rely on fixed passwords to provide secure identities to services or entities.
optionRationales: IAM roles provide temporary, dynamically issued permissions that expire automatically, making them ideal for securely delegating access to services or external accounts.
IAM users are static identities associated with long-term credentials such as passwords or access keys, which increases risk if those credentials are shared with third parties.
IAM groups are used to organize users within the same account and simplify policy assignment; they are not identities that directly make API calls.
An IAM password policy defines complexity and expiration requirements for local human users and does not provide cross-account temporary access.

questions.text: A retail company wants to mitigate application-layer (Layer 7) cyberattacks such as SQL injection and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attempts against its public website. Which AWS service is specifically designed to filter this type of malicious web traffic?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF lets you monitor and filter HTTP/HTTPS requests sent to resources such as Amazon CloudFront and Application Load Balancers, blocking common web-attack patterns.
questions.hint: Look for the firewall specialized in inspecting HTTP and HTTPS request content directly at the web application layer.
optionRationales: AWS WAF lets you monitor and filter HTTP/HTTPS requests sent to resources such as Amazon CloudFront and Application Load Balancers, blocking common web-attack patterns.
AWS Shield Standard works mainly at the network and transport layers, providing automatic baseline protection against common volumetric DDoS attacks.
GuardDuty is an intelligent threat-detection service that analyzes log metadata in the background to identify suspicious account activity; it is not an inline web firewall.
Secrets Manager stores and rotates logical secrets such as database credentials and API keys; it does not filter network requests.

questions.text: A multinational company manages dozens of subsidiaries using AWS Organizations. questions.hint: Think of the structured policies applied at the organization level to restrict what member accounts may or may not do.
optionRationales: Service Control Policies (SCPs) act as centralized guardrails in AWS Organizations by defining the maximum available permissions for member accounts, limiting what local administrators can allow.
Resource-based policies are attached locally to resources such as S3 buckets and may be changed by administrators in the member account, so they are not immutable centralized organization guardrails.
Permission boundaries cap the permissions of individual IAM users and roles, not the maximum permissions of entire member accounts in AWS Organizations.
AWS Network Firewall protects VPC network perimeters against packet-level threats and does not manage logical AWS API permissions.

questions.text: A high-traffic news portal is hosted on AWS and wants protection against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks that try to take the application down by flooding the network with illegitimate traffic at Layers 3 and 4. Which AWS service provides native, automatic protection at no additional charge against common volumetric attacks for all AWS customers?
questions.explanation: AWS Shield Standard is automatically enabled at no additional charge and provides baseline protection against common network- and transport-layer DDoS attacks for AWS customers.
questions.hint: Consider the service that acts as a continuously active background shield protecting AWS's global network infrastructure.
optionRationales: AWS Shield Standard is automatically enabled at no additional charge and provides baseline protection against common network- and transport-layer DDoS attacks for AWS customers.
Shield Advanced is an optional paid service with 24/7 specialized support, financial protections, and additional advanced tooling.
AWS WAF handles HTTP/HTTPS traffic at the application layer (Layer 7), protecting against specific web exploits using configurable rules.

AWS Firewall Manager centralizes the management and enforcement of security rules such as WAF policies and security-group rules across multiple accounts; it is not the baseline free DDoS-protection mechanism.

questions.text: During an IT team restructuring, the IAM administrator needs to give the same read-only access to Amazon RDS to 30 new data analysts. To apply these permissions efficiently and minimize governance overhead, which IAM strategy does AWS recommend?
options: Attach the permissions policy manually to each of the 30 user identities.
Create an IAM group, attach the read policy to the group, and add all 30 users to it.
Generate one shared access key and distribute it by email to the entire team.
Tell the team to sign in simultaneously with the root user to optimize database queries.
questions.explanation: Using IAM groups simplifies access management by allowing permissions for multiple analysts to be changed or revoked in one place instead of managing individual policies for every user.
questions.hint: AWS recommends grouping identities with similar access needs under a common administrative structure to simplify governance.
optionRationales: Using IAM groups simplifies access management by allowing permissions for multiple analysts to be changed or revoked in one place instead of managing individual policies for every user.
Configuring permissions individually increases operational complexity and significantly raises the risk of human error in access governance.
Sharing access keys violates security and audit principles because actions can no longer be reliably attributed to an individual identity.
Using the root user for everyday tasks violates security best practices and exposes unrestricted account permissions to severe risk.

questions.text: An insurance company stores confidential policy backups in an Amazon S3 bucket. Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for configuring bucket access controls, enabling object encryption, and ensuring a secure lifecycle for that data?
options: The AWS Marketplace support team exclusively.
The telecommunications provider supplying the internet connection.
questions.explanation: The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud, which includes protecting their own data, managing identities, and configuring storage access controls and encryption.
questions.hint: Consider who owns and configures the logical assets and files created inside the customer's AWS environment.
optionRationales: The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud, which includes protecting their own data, managing identities, and configuring storage access controls and encryption.

AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud, including physical servers, global networking, and the facilities supporting storage, but AWS does not configure the customer's stored data or bucket permissions.
AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog for purchasing third-party software and is not responsible for managing private S3 buckets created by customers.
Telecommunications providers supply external network connectivity and do not manage logical IAM or S3 permissions configured inside an AWS account.

questions.text: A security engineer is reviewing a company's AWS IAM console and notices that an analyst who left the organization six months ago still has an active IAM user with associated long-term access keys. Which IAM security best practice has been violated?
options: Disable encryption in transit for every Amazon S3 bucket.
Configure strict Network ACL rules to block internet traffic to the console port.
Remove unnecessary credentials and rotate access keys periodically to maintain least privilege.
Use the root user to manage and sign customized tax reports.
questions.explanation: Keeping old, unused credentials active increases the account's exposure. Access for former employees should be revoked immediately and long-term credentials should be reviewed regularly.
questions.hint: Continuous access hygiene includes disabling idle identities and long-lived credentials that no longer serve a business purpose.
optionRationales: Keeping old, unused credentials active increases the account's exposure. Access for former employees should be revoked immediately and long-term credentials should be reviewed regularly.
Network ACLs filter network packets at the VPC subnet layer; they do not disable or audit IAM identities or access keys used to make AWS API requests.
Using the root user for routine work is discouraged and violates fundamental cloud-security best practices.
Disabling encryption would expose sensitive data to interception and directly contradict cybersecurity best practices.

questions.text: A mobile-gaming startup wants to block malicious bots performing automated brute-force attacks against its HTTP login page. The technical team wants flexible rules based on the number of requests from an IP address within a time window. Which AWS service provides this customizable Layer 7 rate-limiting capability?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF supports rate-based rules that count web requests from source IP addresses and can temporarily block addresses that exceed a configured request threshold.
questions.hint: Consider the application firewall designed to inspect HTTP headers, control request rates, and mitigate bots at the web layer.
optionRationales: AWS WAF supports rate-based rules that count web requests from source IP addresses and can temporarily block addresses that exceed a configured request threshold.
AWS Shield Standard provides background protection against common large-scale network attacks but does not provide granular bot filtering for specific HTTP URLs.
Route 53 health checks monitor endpoint health and availability for DNS routing; they do not filter injection attacks or brute-force requests.
AWS KMS creates and manages cryptographic keys for protecting data at rest and does not filter network connections or HTTP requests.

questions.text: The security team at a digital bank wants to track and audit every action performed in its corporate AWS account, such as terminating an EC2 instance or creating an IAM user. The team needs a historical record containing the user identity, source IP address, and time of each command. Which AWS service records this control-plane activity history?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail continuously records AWS account activity and API calls, providing a detailed audit trail that is essential for security investigations and compliance.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS service whose audit mission is to record who did what, when, and from where through AWS API activity.
optionRationales: AWS CloudTrail continuously records AWS account activity and API calls, providing a detailed audit trail that is essential for security investigations and compliance.
Amazon CloudWatch focuses on operational monitoring, performance metrics such as CPU utilization, and centralized application and operating-system logs.
AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates the environment against AWS best practices and provides recommendations, but it is not the raw forensic recorder of API transactions.
AWS Config records resource configurations and tracks configuration changes, inventory, and relationships among AWS resources rather than serving as the primary API-call audit trail.

questions.text: A company wants to align its IT infrastructure with the principle of least privilege from the AWS Well-Architected Framework. When creating a new JSON IAM permissions policy for its support team, which approach should the administrator take?
options: Use wildcard permissions across all actions and resources to simplify the team's API calls.
Delegate the root-user credentials so the team can resolve incidents without permission barriers.
Grant AdministratorAccess temporarily and revoke it only after a critical security incident occurs.
Grant only the minimum permissions required for analysts to perform their job responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The principle of least privilege requires users and applications to receive only the permissions strictly necessary for their normal tasks, reducing the potential blast radius of mistakes or compromise.
questions.hint: This security principle recommends limiting legitimate access as much as possible and granting only the actions needed for routine work.
optionRationales: The principle of least privilege requires users and applications to receive only the permissions strictly necessary for their normal tasks, reducing the potential blast radius of mistakes or compromise.
Granting full access for convenience violates core security principles and leaves the environment exposed to accidental or intentional destructive actions.
Global wildcard permissions grant unrestricted privileges across account services, which is the opposite of granular least-privilege access.
Sharing root credentials exposes full account control and violates established cybersecurity best practices.

questions.text: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, who is responsible for the physical integrity and perimeter security of AWS data-center facilities, uninterrupted power systems, and secure disposal of retired storage media?
options: AWS exclusively, as part of security OF the cloud.
The AWS Artifact Enterprise Hub committee.
The AWS customer, as part of security IN the cloud.
Local internet service providers and mobile network operators.
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for managing and physically protecting the underlying hardware, facilities, utilities, and infrastructure that support the AWS Cloud.
questions.hint: Physical servers, racks, cooling systems, building security, and disposal of physical media are responsibilities of the cloud provider.
optionRationales: AWS is responsible for managing and physically protecting the underlying hardware, facilities, utilities, and infrastructure that support the AWS Cloud.
Customers are responsible for logical security inside their accounts, including permissions, stored data, and software updates on the resources they manage.
Telecommunications providers supply external network connectivity and do not control physical security inside AWS facilities.
AWS Artifact is a self-service repository for compliance reports and agreements; it does not provide physical data-center security.

questions.text: A cloud engineer is configuring consolidated billing for a conglomerate using AWS Organizations. For geographic compliance, the company wants a Service Control Policy (SCP) that restricts resource creation to the São Paulo Region. options: At the organization root or to specific Organizational Units (OUs) in AWS Organizations.
To the virtual network interfaces (ENIs) of each individual instance in VPC subnets.
Inside AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
In the local IAM password policy for human users.
questions.explanation: SCPs are centralized guardrails in AWS Organizations and can be attached to the organization root or Organizational Units so their restrictions are inherited by member accounts.
questions.hint: Think of the centralized hierarchical console used to manage multiple accounts, consolidated billing, and organization-wide permission guardrails.
optionRationales: SCPs are centralized guardrails in AWS Organizations and can be attached to the organization root or Organizational Units so their restrictions are inherited by member accounts.
Elastic Network Interfaces use controls such as security groups for network traffic; they cannot interpret organization-level SCP permissions.
Parameter Store manages application configuration values and secrets-like strings; it does not enforce organization-wide AWS API permission boundaries.
IAM password policies define password complexity and expiration requirements for users and do not control geographic Region permissions.

questions.text: A startup wants an additional protection layer for its web application against brute-force attacks targeting login pages. The team wants to inspect strings and character patterns contained in incoming HTTP request bodies and create rules that block malicious requests. Which AWS service provides this advanced application-layer inspection?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF can inspect incoming Layer 7 traffic in detail and lets you create rules based on text patterns found in HTTP headers, cookies, and request bodies.

optionRationales: AWS WAF can inspect incoming Layer 7 traffic in detail and lets you create rules based on text patterns found in HTTP headers, cookies, and request bodies.
AWS Shield Standard automatically protects against common volumetric network and transport-layer attacks but does not inspect application-level text inside HTTP requests.
GuardDuty analyzes security telemetry and can provide malware-related findings, but it is not an inline HTTP request firewall.
Systems Manager Run Command remotely executes administrative commands on managed compute resources and does not filter perimeter web traffic.

questions.text: An external compliance auditor asks a Brazilian startup for formally signed documents and independent third-party audit reports proving that AWS global infrastructure meets standards such as ISO 27001 and SOC 2. questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is AWS's central self-service resource for downloading third-party compliance reports, security certifications, and managing certain agreements directly through the AWS console.
questions.hint: Consider the AWS self-service portal designed specifically for compliance artifacts, audit reports, and official agreements.
optionRationales: AWS Artifact is AWS's central self-service resource for downloading third-party compliance reports, security certifications, and managing certain agreements directly through the AWS console.
AWS Config evaluates and records the configuration state of customer resources but does not provide AWS's global third-party audit reports.
There is no official AWS service named 'AWS Trust Premium Portal.'
AWS CloudTrail records API activity in the customer's account for auditing and forensic analysis, but it is not a repository for international compliance certification reports.

questions.text: The security team at a healthcare provider wants continuous monitoring of its AWS account to identify suspicious or malicious activity, such as cryptocurrency mining attempts on Amazon EC2 instances or API calls originating from impossible geographic locations. Which managed service consumes network and account logs and uses native intelligence to detect these threats automatically?
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a continuous intelligent threat-detection service that analyzes security telemetry such as VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and AWS CloudTrail events, using machine learning and threat intelligence to identify potentially malicious activity.
questions.hint: Think of the intelligent security service that behaves like a continuous guard, detecting suspicious activity from telemetry and anomalous behavior.
optionRationales: Amazon GuardDuty is a continuous intelligent threat-detection service that analyzes security telemetry such as VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and AWS CloudTrail events, using machine learning and threat intelligence to identify potentially malicious activity.

AWS Shield Advanced is focused on advanced mitigation of complex volumetric DDoS attacks at the network and transport layers; it is not a general behavior-based threat-detection service for account activity.
AWS WAF works inline at the application layer by inspecting and filtering HTTP/HTTPS requests at Layer 7 for public web applications.

Amazon Inspector performs automated vulnerability scanning for software packages, container images, and supported compute resources; it does not primarily hunt for threats based on network and API behavior.

questions.text: A retail company needs to encrypt at rest all data stored in Amazon EBS volumes and S3 buckets. The governance team requires a centralized solution where cryptographic keys, their lifecycle, and access policies are managed natively and key activity can be audited through AWS CloudTrail. Which AWS service provides this centralized key management?
questions.explanation: AWS KMS lets customers create and manage KMS keys through a fully managed centralized service and integrates natively with many AWS services to protect data at rest.

AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store stores configuration values and SecureString parameters, but it is not the primary service for creating and managing the encryption keys used by storage services.

questions.text: A security architect needs strict network controls for fleets of EC2 instances inside an Amazon VPC. The architect wants rules that act as a stateful virtual firewall and filter traffic directly at the elastic network interface (ENI) level of each individual server. Which VPC security component provides this behavior?

questions.text: The IT director of an insurance company wants to continuously audit the configuration of resources in its AWS account. AWS KMS manages cryptographic keys used to encrypt data; it is not an application-secret vault for storing passwords and API tokens.
AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements for audit and regulatory purposes; it is not a secret-management service.

questions.text: A junior network engineer is configuring perimeter rules for a private subnet in an Amazon VPC. The engineer needs a security component that acts as a stateless firewall at the subnet boundary and evaluates inbound and outbound traffic through numbered ordered rules. AWS WAF filters Layer 7 HTTP/HTTPS requests for supported web resources and does not manage VPC subnet port rules.
An Internet Gateway provides routing between public VPC subnets and the internet; it is not a stateless numbered-rule firewall.

questions.text: A company wants to centralize stable configuration variables and non-sensitive strings, such as development database URLs and logical bucket names, in a hierarchical and scalable way without a fixed monthly charge per standard parameter. Which AWS Systems Manager capability best fits this simple configuration-management scenario?
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store stores configuration parameters and strings in hierarchical paths and supports standard parameters without a per-parameter monthly storage fee.
questions.hint: Consider the Systems Manager repository designed for lightweight storage of application parameters and configuration strings.
optionRationales: AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store stores configuration parameters and strings in hierarchical paths and supports standard parameters without a per-parameter monthly storage fee.
AWS Secrets Manager is designed for sensitive secrets and automated rotation and carries a recurring per-secret charge, which is unnecessary for simple non-sensitive configuration values.
AWS KMS manages cryptographic keys used to encrypt data and is not a hierarchical text repository for application configuration paths.
AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and audit documents about AWS controls and facilities; it does not store application configuration parameters.

questions.text: During a preventive cybersecurity audit, a startup discovers that a public Amazon S3 bucket accidentally exposes sensitive files because of a developer misconfiguration. The team wants a native automated data-security and privacy service that continuously analyzes S3 data using pattern matching and machine learning to identify and alert on personally identifiable information (PII), such as credit-card numbers or national identification data. Which service meets this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and privacy service that uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and help protect sensitive data stored in Amazon S3.

AWS Config evaluates the configuration state and compliance of AWS resources; it does not inspect the internal contents of S3 objects for sensitive information.
AWS Trusted Advisor may flag certain resource risks and best-practice issues, but it does not read and classify sensitive content inside documents stored in S3.

questions.text: A large healthcare organization uses Amazon RDS to host a relational database containing patient records. Symmetric key obfuscation through AWS Artifact.

AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements; it does not implement network-channel encryption mechanisms.
EC2 Instance Store provides temporary local block storage attached to compute hosts and is unrelated to network transport encryption protocols.

questions.text: A solutions architect at a fintech company wants to restrict administrative access to a production EC2 server hosted in a public Amazon VPC subnet. The architect needs a rule that explicitly denies all inbound traffic originating from a known block of public IP addresses. Which VPC network component supports an explicit Deny rule for IP ranges?

Security groups support allow rules only. Traffic that is not explicitly allowed is denied implicitly, but you cannot add an explicit per-IP Deny rule to a security group.
Systems Manager Parameter Store stores application configuration strings and parameters; it is not a network firewall.
AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for compliance reports and agreements and does not inspect or block network traffic.

questions.text: A company runs a web server continuously, 24 hours a day and 7 days a week, with a stable and predictable workload throughout the year. Which Amazon EC2 pricing model offers the largest structural discount for this predictable long-term usage pattern?

questions.hint: Consider the model that exchanges predictable long-term usage and a time commitment for reduced compute rates.
optionRationales: Reserved Instances can provide significant discounts compared with On-Demand pricing in exchange for a 1-year or 3-year commitment to a consistent amount of EC2 usage.

Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity at deep discounts but can be interrupted, making them unsuitable for a workload that must run continuously without unexpected termination.
Dedicated Hosts allocate an entire physical server to a customer for licensing or compliance scenarios and usually cost more than standard committed EC2 purchasing options.

questions.text: A backend developer needs to store monthly PDF reports that are accessed frequently during their first few weeks but are rarely accessed afterward. S3 Standard-IA is designed for infrequently accessed data that still requires millisecond access when requested, at a lower storage price than S3 Standard.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is a low-cost archive class, but retrieval can take minutes to hours and therefore does not satisfy the immediate-download requirement.
S3 One Zone-IA is cheaper but stores data in a single Availability Zone, which provides less resilience than S3 Standard-IA for important financial or compliance records.

questions.text: A network engineer is configuring a new two-tier Amazon VPC for a web application and database. The EC2 instances hosting the public frontend must be able to send and receive traffic directly to and from the public internet. questions.explanation: An Internet Gateway is the horizontally scaled VPC component that enables communication between resources in public subnets and the public internet when routing and addressing are configured appropriately.

An Internet Gateway is the horizontally scaled VPC component that enables communication between resources in public subnets and the public internet when routing and addressing are configured appropriately.
A Virtual Private Gateway is associated with private VPN connectivity between a VPC and external networks such as on-premises environments rather than general internet access.

questions.text: A startup wants to deploy a traditional web application backed by a SQL relational database. Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that automates many routine operational tasks such as provisioning, backups, monitoring, and database software maintenance for supported engines.

questions.text: A software architect is building a microservice that processes short text logs whenever a new file is uploaded. The architect wants event-driven serverless computing, payment based on actual code execution time, automatic scaling, and no continuously running virtual servers to manage. optionRationales: Amazon EC2 provides traditional virtual servers that remain billable while running and require the customer to manage the guest operating system.
AWS Lambda is AWS's serverless compute service for running code in response to events, with automatic scaling and no server infrastructure for the developer to provision or manage.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk is a managed application deployment platform, but it commonly provisions underlying resources such as EC2 instances that remain running continuously.
Amazon ECS orchestrates containers and can use different compute options, but ECS itself is not the short-function serverless execution model described by the requirement.

questions.text: A developer is running short-lived tests for a new mobile application on Amazon EC2. The workload can consume substantial compute at unpredictable times but can tolerate temporary interruptions without business impact. To maximize savings by using spare AWS compute capacity, which EC2 purchasing model should be selected?

questions.hint: Focus on the EC2 option that offers deep discounts for workloads that can tolerate being interrupted when AWS needs the spare capacity back.
optionRationales: On-Demand Instances offer flexibility without a long-term commitment but are billed at standard rates and do not provide the deep discounts associated with spare capacity.

Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity and can provide very large discounts compared with On-Demand pricing. They are appropriate for interruption-tolerant workloads such as flexible tests and batch processing.
Reserved Instances are intended for predictable long-term usage commitments and are not ideal for short, sporadic tests with highly variable demand.

questions.text: An IT analyst wants objects in an Amazon S3 bucket to be moved automatically to a cheaper long-term archive storage class after they are more than 90 days old. Which native S3 feature manages these time-based storage transitions automatically?

questions.hint: Think of the feature that manages the stages of an object's life from creation through archival or eventual expiration.
optionRationales: S3 Object Lock protects objects from deletion or overwrite for retention and compliance purposes; it does not automate storage-class transitions.

questions.text: While creating an isolated network in Amazon VPC, an administrator needs to divide the VPC's main IP address range into smaller segments so internal database servers can be separated from public web servers. questions.text: A company wants to understand the difference between on-premises infrastructure and the AWS Cloud from a cost-model perspective. What is the primary difference between these two models?

On-premises infrastructure typically requires CAPEX, such as upfront hardware investment, while AWS supports an OPEX-oriented pay-as-you-go model that replaces large upfront investment with variable cost based on actual usage.
